newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Paccar of U.S. launches bid for Dutch DAF Trucks.
newsitem.headline: Paccar of U.S. launches bid for Dutch DAF Trucks.

text.p: U.S. truck-maker Paccar Inc has made a 933 million guilder ($543.8 million) bid to take over the privately held Dutch company DAF Trucks NV, DAF said on Monday.
DAF Trucks is the successor company to DAF NV which was declared bankrupt in 1993. Its single biggest shareholder is the Dutch government with a stake of just under 40 percent.
DAF Trucks said Paccar's takeover offer had the support of DAF's two main management organs, the executive board and the supervisory board. The offer will close on November 15.
The Dutch company described Paccar as the world's third largest producer of heavy trucks, with a 1995 output of over 54,000 vehicles.
DAF Trucks made over 16,600 vehicles at its Eindhoven plant in 1995 and claims a nine percent shares of the West European market for trucks heavier than 15 tonnes.
Paccar has four plants in the U.S. and has over 20 percent of the North American market for heavy trucks.
The company, which makes trucks under the Peterbilt, Kenworth and Foden brand names, also has production facilities in Britain, Australia and Mexico.
DAF Trucks quoted its chairman Cor Baan as saying that the synergies created by the takeover would make a stronger whole.
"Together we will have greater innovative power and technological possibilities," he said.
Baan said Paccar planned to run DAF Trucks as an independent unit, retaining the DAF and Leyland DAF brand names.
Paccar made a net profit of $253 million on sales of $4.6 billion in 1995. DAF Trucks made a net profit of 164 million guilders on sales of 2.9 billion guilders in the same year.

DAF Trucks said the overall bid of 933 million guilders included an amount of 33 million guilders for a 25 percent stake in its Belgian unit held by Flemish regional institutions. ($ = 1.715 Dutch Guilders)
